jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Forty Years
jokes.joke: I built a time machine and went back to summer camp to stop myself from performing in the talent show. I told twelve-year-old me, “Trust me, this will embarrass you for forty years.” He lit up: “I live past fifty?” Then he ran onstage like I’d just given him a standing ovation.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: The Time Machine Boyfriend
jokes.joke: I dated a guy who claimed he could time travel. Never proved it, but boy could he use it. Every fight somehow became about something I did in 2019. 'This is just like when you canceled on me in 2019.' I don't even remember 2019, man, but apparently I owe you an apology from the past. He wasn't a time traveler. He was just really good at dragging me there.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Cabin Fever
jokes.joke: I got sent to a sleepaway camp run by joyless survivalists who treated eight-year-olds like conscripts. Day two, I tried cracking a joke to break the ice during mandatory silent breakfast, and the head counselor stared right through my soul and said, 'Laughter burns calories you haven't earned today.' I didn't smile again until my parents picked me up in August.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Camp Royalty
jokes.joke: When I was at summer camp, there was this charming kid who convinced the whole cabin he was a European prince. We made his bed, carried his backpack, gave him the best bunk. Then visiting day came and his mom pulled up in a rusty minivan from Ohio yelling, 'Tommy, get your butt in the car!' So much for nobility.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Early Arrival
jokes.joke: I tried revisiting the summer camp I went to as a kid, and the place felt frozen in time. Same cabins, same lake, same counselor yelling at me for being late. I said, “I’m thirty-five now, does it still count?” He said, “Absolutely. You were supposed to be here at 9.” That’s when I realized time travel is real—I’m still getting in trouble for the same stuff decades later.
